theme: Head-final and head-initial seal-legend comparison corpora and the head-direction discrimination test
question: Which seal-legend statistics, at sign and word level, separate head-final from head-initial languages consistently across at least two corpora of each, measured with the same code on legends that each link to an object and a site?
outcome: Built object- and site-linked corpora: Indo-Aryan seals and sealings from Basarh and Bhita (556 records, 245 eligible distinct legends at sign level, 30 at word level), Tamil-Brahmi seals, rings and coins (31 records, 23 and 7), Ur III Sumerian seal legends (31,512 records, 3,044 and 3,026) and Old Akkadian legends in Akkadian (89 records, 11 and 10). The frozen keep rule needs two corpora of each group with at least 25 eligible legends; only one of each entered, at threshold 25 and in the declared panel at 20, so no statistic was kept or rejected. Descriptively, at matched size 196 Indo-Aryan and Ur III separate in every draw: edge asymmetry +0.250 against -0.219, closing concentration 0.628 against 0.204, stock closure beyond shuffle +0.264 against -0.025, word-internal asymmetry +0.204 against -0.111; Tamil-Brahmi sits with Indo-Aryan at n = 18 (+0.363). The 11 Akkadian legends also end in few signs (edge asymmetry +0.134 beyond their shuffle range -0.073 to +0.092). An exploratory count after the runs puts titles before names in 57 of 61 Indo-Aryan pairs and after names in 2,393 of 2,475 Ur III pairs and 10 of 15 Akkadian pairs.
challenge: Few Akkadian-language seal legends of the Old Akkadian period have a site and an undamaged edge; few Tamil-Brahmi seals and rings were published by 2003; Gupta legends are mostly one compound word, so the head-final word level is thin. No lawful digital copy of Avigad and Sass 1997 was found. The editors print restorations and corrections in different bracket conventions, the delegated transliteration mapping turned aspirates into c, and 25 CDLI seal records are composite editions without a physical object.
remedy: Protocol, schema and transcription brief hashed before transcription; four amendments hashed before computation fix the unit rules, the transliteration by source, each editor's bracket conventions (checked on page images), the code corrections, the exclusions and a second panel at threshold 20. Both runs computed every statistic on the entering corpora as description, with shuffle references, sub-corpora and two sensitivity runs. The feasibility ledger lists the routes to the missing corpora.
retry_when: At least 25 eligible Akkadian (or other head-initial, such as West Semitic) seal legends with object and site, and at least 25 eligible Tamil-Brahmi seal and ring legends, are normalised to SCHEMA.md; run the frozen protocol unchanged at threshold 25 with the compound members of Indo-Aryan legends as word units. A new seed over these corpora supplies no new evidence.
authors: Codex CLI 0.160.1 with GPT-6.1-Sol (gpt-6.1-sol, reasoning effort xhigh)
